info.name: SIRMS v1 - Service 3 - Incident Management (Karim Hajj Ali)
info.description:
Incident Management under team-integration-v1.0.0, on port 8003.
Authentication under team-integration-v1.0.0
--------------------------------------------
There is no login request in these collections. Natalio's Users service is
the only token issuer:

    POST {{users_url}}/users/login
    {"identifier": "your.username", "password": "..."}

Take `data.access_token` from his response and paste it into the
`admin_token` / `analyst_token` environment variable. Tokens last 1800
seconds. Never commit a filled-in environment.

The internal collection uses service credentials instead, not a user
token: `X-Service-Name` plus `X-Service-Key`, with a fresh
`Idempotency-Key` per delivery (Postman's {{$guid}} generates one).

Request templates for the named-route update. No execution responses captured. Original earlier captures are under postman/historical/pre-v1.1/.

request.description: Report an incident. Administrator or Regular Employee. An employee is always recorded as their own reporter.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Ransomware detected on domain controller",
  "description": "Encryption activity flagged on the domain controller.",
  "category": "Malware Infection",
  "severity": "Critical",
  "affected_asset": 1
}

request.description: Complete list. Administrator or Auditor. This is the shape Chris's Reports consumes: body.incidents with a success status and count.
One incident with its investigation notes. An employee may only read an incident they reported.
Administrator only. The target's role is checked against Users over HTTP, so a demoted account is refused. Queues an Incident Assignment notification.
One step along Open -> Under Investigation -> Mitigated -> Resolved -> Closed. Skipping a step is refused with 400 naming the only allowed next status.
Administrator or Analyst. Returned as part of GET /incidents/{id}.
Readiness of this service, including whether its own tables can be queried.
